title: T2-RELION: Task Parallelism, Tensor Core Accelerated RELION for Cryo-EM 3D Reconstruction
problem: RELION's computational efficiency during cryo-EM 3D reconstruction remains a bottleneck due to inefficient parallelization strategies and suboptimal GPU memory management.
motivation: Cryo-electron microscopy is critical for structural biology but computationally intensive. Optimizing RELION on GPU-accelerated platforms can significantly accelerate 3D reconstruction workflows.
method: Optimized RELION implementation introducing: task-level parallelism, three-phase GPU memory management strategy, and Tensor Core acceleration for difference calculation kernels with advanced pipelining for latency hiding and data reuse.
key_novelty: First application of task parallelism and Tensor Core acceleration to RELION, combined with memory hierarchy optimization for efficient GPU utilization on CPU-GPU platforms.
contributions: Task parallelism redesign improving RELION parallelization efficiency
Tensor Core acceleration of difference calculation kernel
Advanced pipelining for latency hiding and thread-block-level data reuse
3.86x and 2.68x application-level speedups on CNG and Trpv1 datasets
limitations: Evaluation limited to two datasets (CNG, Trpv1); specificity to NVIDIA A100 may limit portability; scalability to larger GPU clusters not fully explored.
